meta.title: Everyday American English Expressions — 500
meta.description: 500 originally authored expressions. TOEFL + Daily denotes potential study usefulness only, not measured exam frequency or externally verified CEFR. Human audio and independent review pending.

cards.usageNote: Used when clothing or heat prevents someone from feeling cold.
examples: This coat will keep you warm on the walk.
A hot drink can help keep you warm outside.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will this sweater be enough?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, it'll keep you warm.

cards.usageNote: Said when you are already traveling to someone or somewhere.
examples: I'm on my way to the station now.
Don't leave yet; I'm on my way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you still at home?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, I'm on my way.

cards.usageNote: Leaves the decision to the other person.
examples: We can eat out or cook; it's up to you.
It's up to you which movie we watch.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we go early?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's up to you.

cards.usageNote: Tells someone there is no need to hurry.
examples: Take your time with the application.
There's no rush, so take your time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sorry, I'm not ready.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No problem. Take your time.

cards.usageNote: Shows agreement with a suggestion or plan.
examples: Seven o'clock sounds good to me.
A short break sounds good to me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How about coffee after work?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sounds good to me.

cards.usageNote: Asks someone to provide an update or decision.
examples: Let me know when you get home.
Please let me know if the time changes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you come on Friday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'll let you know tonight.

cards.usageNote: Expresses not wanting to do a particular activity.
examples: I'm not in the mood for a big party.
She's not in the mood to talk right now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Want to watch a horror movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm not in the mood for that.

cards.usageNote: Said when a kind act or news makes you very happy.
examples: Your message really made my day.
That compliment made my day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I brought your favorite cake.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oh, you made my day!

cards.usageNote: Shows you understand someone's explanation.
examples: That makes sense now that you've explained it.
Your decision makes sense to me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We left early to avoid traffic.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That makes sense.

cards.usageNote: Said when it is difficult to control an action or feeling.
examples: I laugh when I'm nervous; I can't help it.
I know I worry too much, but I can't help it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why are you smiling?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I can't help it; I'm excited.

cards.usageNote: Casual reassurance after an apology or thanks.
examples: No worries, I can send it again.
No worries about being a few minutes late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sorry I missed your call.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No worries.

cards.usageNote: Said when handing something to someone.
examples: Here you go, your receipt is in the bag.
Here you go, I found your keys.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Could I have some water?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sure, here you go.

cards.usageNote: Says you do not know the answer.
examples: I have no idea where the charger went.
I have no idea what time the store closes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Who's at the door?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I have no idea.

cards.usageNote: Explains a precaution taken for a possible situation.
examples: Bring an umbrella just in case.
I saved a copy just in case the file disappears.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why did you pack a jacket?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Just in case it gets cold.

cards.usageNote: Asks for or promises prompt action without a fixed deadline.
examples: Please reply as soon as possible.
I'll send the documents as soon as possible.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: When can you fix it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: As soon as possible.

cards.usageNote: Describes a temporary arrangement.
examples: For the time being, I'm working from home.
We can use this room for the time being.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you moving out?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not yet; I'll stay here for the time being.

cards.usageNote: Describes something happening occasionally.
examples: We go hiking from time to time.
From time to time, I call an old friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you still play tennis?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: From time to time.

cards.usageNote: Downplays a small problem or inconvenience.
examples: It's not a big deal if we're a little late.
The scratch is tiny; it's not a big deal.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I forgot the napkins.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's not a big deal.

cards.usageNote: Asks for clarification of someone's words.
examples: What do you mean by a different plan?
Sorry, what do you mean exactly?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We need to change everything.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: What do you mean?

cards.usageNote: Checks whether someone is confident about something.
examples: Are you sure this is the right address?
Are you sure you don't want help?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The meeting starts at nine.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Are you sure?

cards.usageNote: Says you have no objection or preference.
examples: I don't mind waiting a few more minutes.
I don't mind if we sit outside.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Would you mind taking the bus?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, I don't mind.

cards.usageNote: Says the answer changes according to circumstances.
examples: It depends on the weather.
Whether I can join depends on my schedule.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will you be there?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It depends on work.

cards.usageNote: Encourages attempting something despite uncertainty.
examples: The recipe is new, but it's worth a try.
Applying for the course is worth a try.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Think this will work?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm not sure, but it's worth a try.

cards.usageNote: Requests a brief moment to do something.
examples: Give me a second to find my wallet.
Give me a second; I'm finishing a message.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you answer now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Give me a second.

cards.usageNote: Says you will arrive later than expected.
examples: I'm running late because of traffic.
Sorry, I'm running late for our meeting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Where are you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm running late, but I'll be there soon.

cards.usageNote: Said when a long time has passed since an event.
examples: It's been a while since we last talked.
It's been a while since I cooked at home.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nice to see you!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's been a while.

cards.usageNote: Asks about a situation or current events.
examples: What's going on outside the office?
I heard a noise; what's going on?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Everyone looks worried.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: What's going on?

cards.usageNote: Says a situation is progressing well up to now.
examples: The first week has been busy, but so far, so good.
We've had no delays; so far, so good.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How's your trip?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: So far, so good.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges another person's point of view.
examples: I see what you mean about the price.
After your example, I see what you mean.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's too crowded at noon.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I see what you mean.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges a useful argument or observation.
examples: That's a good point about the budget.
You raised a good point about timing.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We might need more chairs.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a good point.

cards.usageNote: Explains that an action was not intentional.
examples: I didn't mean to interrupt you.
I didn't mean to sound rude.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You scared me!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sorry, I didn't mean to.

cards.usageNote: Casual admission of a small mistake.
examples: My bad, I sent the wrong photo.
My bad, I read the time incorrectly.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You took my seat.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: My bad! I'll move.

cards.tr: Hazırım; başka bir şeye ihtiyacım yok
cards.usageNote: Indicates readiness or that no more help is needed.
examples: I'm all set for tomorrow's trip.
Thanks, I'm all set with my order.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Anything else for you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No thanks, I'm all set.

cards.usageNote: Accepts an arrangement or solution.
examples: Tuesday afternoon works for me.
A video call works for me instead.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we meet online?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That works for me.

cards.usageNote: Says you will return shortly.
examples: I'll be right back with the menu.
Wait here; I'll be right back.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Where are you going?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'll be right back.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a clarification to prevent misunderstanding.
examples: Don't get me wrong, I like the idea.
Don't get me wrong; I'm grateful for your help.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You don't like the restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Don't get me wrong, I do.

cards.usageNote: Introduces an honest personal opinion.
examples: To be honest, I'm exhausted.
To be honest, the movie was too long.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you enjoy it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: To be honest, not much.

cards.usageNote: Introduces an opinion, often informally.
examples: If you ask me, we should leave earlier.
The blue one looks better, if you ask me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Which route is best?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: If you ask me, the highway.

cards.usageNote: Accepts something proposed by another person.
examples: If you want to wait, that's fine with me.
That's fine with me as long as we finish today.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we change seats?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's fine with me.

cards.usageNote: Politely declines an action.
examples: I'd rather not drive tonight.
I'd rather not discuss it now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Want to go out?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'd rather not tonight.

cards.usageNote: Expresses positive anticipation of a future event.
examples: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
We're looking forward to meeting you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: See you on Saturday!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm looking forward to it.

cards.usageNote: Welcomes a guest and invites them to relax.
examples: Come in and make yourself at home.
Make yourself at home while I make tea.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should I take my shoes off?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, then make yourself at home.

cards.usageNote: Invites someone to take food or another offered item.
examples: Help yourself to some coffee.
Please help yourself to the snacks.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I have a cookie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Of course, help yourself.

cards.usageNote: Clarifies that a remark was meant as a joke.
examples: I'm just kidding; you did a great job.
Don't worry, I'm just kidding about the bill.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You sold my bike?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, I'm just kidding!

cards.usageNote: Concedes that another person's argument has merit.
examples: You've got a point about the traffic.
You've got a point; we should compare prices.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We could take a train.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You've got a point.

cards.usageNote: Signals understanding of something.
examples: I get it now; the password expired.
I get it, you're trying to help.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The entrance is around the back.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oh, I get it.

cards.usageNote: Suggests ending work or an activity for the day.
examples: We've finished the report; let's call it a day.
It's getting late; let's call it a day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: One more task?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, let's call it a day.

cards.usageNote: Offers to pay for something.
examples: Dinner is on me tonight.
Don't pay for the coffee; it's on me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Who pays for lunch?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's on me.

cards.usageNote: Politely declines an offer in casual American English.
examples: I'm good, thanks; I already ate.
No dessert for me, I'm good, thanks.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Would you like more tea?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm good, thanks.

cards.usageNote: Expresses relief after worry or tension.
examples: What a relief that everyone is safe.
The test was canceled? What a relief!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The package arrived.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: What a relief!

cards.usageNote: Says a possibility cannot be ruled out.
examples: Pack a snack; you never know.
You never know who might need help.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you think it'll rain?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You never know.

cards.usageNote: Says doing something late is better than not doing it.
examples: You finally called—better late than never.
She started learning at forty; better late than never.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I finally finished the book.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Better late than never.

cards.usageNote: Says you do not have the right to interfere.
examples: It's none of my business how they spend money.
I won't ask; it's none of my business.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why didn't you ask about it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's none of my business.

cards.usageNote: Says a decision or fact is not settled.
examples: I'm not sure yet whether I can come.
I'm not sure yet about my plans.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you joining us?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm not sure yet.

cards.usageNote: Gives a mild negative answer.
examples: Not really; I prefer staying in.
I don't really feel tired—well, not really.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you like spicy food?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not really.

cards.usageNote: Strongly confirms or agrees.
examples: Absolutely, I can help with that.
You should absolutely try this soup.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I sit here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Absolutely.

cards.usageNote: Strongly denies or reassures.
examples: Of course not; I didn't forget you.
Of course not, that won't be a problem.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you upset with me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Of course not.

cards.usageNote: Emphasizes a denial or politely replies to thanks.
examples: I'm not tired at all.
Not at all; it was my pleasure.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did I bother you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not at all.

cards.usageNote: Confident informal agreement.
examples: I'll be there for sure.
That's one place I'd visit for sure.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you coming tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: For sure.

cards.usageNote: Accepts another person's reason or position.
examples: Fair enough, we can postpone it.
Your concern is fair enough.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I need to save money.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Fair enough.

cards.usageNote: Congratulates someone, though tone can make it sarcastic.
examples: You got promoted? Good for you!
Good for you for finishing the course.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I started exercising again.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Good for you!

cards.usageNote: Says an explanation would take a long time.
examples: Why I moved is a long story.
It's a long story, but I'll tell you later.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How did you meet?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's a long story.

cards.expression: To make a long story short
cards.usageNote: Introduces a short summary of a longer story.
examples: To make a long story short, we missed the train.
To make a long story short, everything worked out.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What happened next?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: To make a long story short, we left.

cards.usageNote: Expresses an intuition without certainty.
examples: I have a feeling it'll rain tonight.
I have a feeling she's planning a surprise.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will they win?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I have a feeling they will.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a related thought or memory.
examples: That reminds me, I need to call Mom.
Your story reminds me of my first job.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We need milk.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That reminds me, I need eggs.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a related topic after something mentioned.
examples: Speaking of which, did you buy tickets?
Speaking of which, how's your sister?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I saw Sam yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Speaking of which, how is he?

cards.usageNote: Limits a statement to what you know.
examples: As far as I know, the store is open.
As far as I know, they live nearby.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is Mia coming?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: As far as I know, yes.

cards.usageNote: Signals uncertainty in a specific recollection.
examples: If I'm not mistaken, we met last year.
If I'm not mistaken, the exit is to the left.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is the meeting at noon?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: If I'm not mistaken, yes.

cards.usageNote: Describes something done just before a deadline.
examples: He canceled at the last minute.
I bought a gift at the last minute.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: When did they change the plan?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: At the last minute.

cards.usageNote: Describes what happens while waiting for something else.
examples: Dinner will be ready soon; in the meantime, set the table.
I'll call them; in the meantime, you can wait here.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The doctor is busy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'll read in the meantime.

cards.usageNote: Encourages gradual progress rather than rushing.
examples: Let's solve this one step at a time.
I'm learning one step at a time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How will we finish this?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: One step at a time.

cards.usageNote: Says something is not worth the effort or risk.
examples: Arguing over five dollars isn't worth it.
Don't drive in that storm; it's not worth it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we wait two hours?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, it's not worth it.

cards.usageNote: Expresses very strong agreement.
examples: I couldn't agree more with your suggestion.
That's exactly right; I couldn't agree more.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We need a break.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I couldn't agree more.

cards.usageNote: Says something is not relevant to the main issue.
examples: The price is beside the point right now.
That's beside the point; we need a decision.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: But I called yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's beside the point.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a qualification or contrasting thought.
examples: The job is demanding. That being said, I enjoy it.
It's expensive. That being said, the quality is excellent.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So you dislike it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not exactly. That being said, I'd choose another one.

cards.usageNote: Says you depend on someone for help or support.
examples: I'm counting on you to be on time.
We're counting on you for the presentation.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will you finish the slides?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, you can count on me.

cards.usageNote: Promises reliability or support.
examples: You can count on me when things get tough.
You can count on me to bring the supplies.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you help us tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You can count on me.

cards.usageNote: Says you cannot control the outcome.
examples: The final decision is out of my hands.
I'd help, but it's out of my hands now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you change the schedule?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's out of my hands.

cards.usageNote: Promises updates as a situation develops.
examples: I'll keep you posted about the delivery.
I'll keep you posted if the meeting changes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Any news on the repair?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not yet, but I'll keep you posted.

cards.usageNote: Says people understand or agree on a plan.
examples: We're on the same page about the budget.
Let's make sure we're on the same page.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do we agree on the deadline?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, we're on the same page.

cards.usageNote: Suggests working together to solve a problem.
examples: We don't know the route; let's figure it out.
Let's figure it out before we call anyone.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The app isn't working.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's figure it out.

cards.expression: It's not the end of the world
cards.usageNote: Says a setback is manageable.
examples: Missing one train isn't the end of the world.
It's not the end of the world if we have to retry.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I failed the quiz.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's not the end of the world.

cards.usageNote: Encourages someone facing difficulty.
examples: Hang in there; the week is almost over.
I know it's hard, but hang in there.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'm exhausted.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hang in there, you'll get a break soon.

cards.usageNote: Encourages rest or a relaxed approach.
examples: Take it easy after your surgery.
You should take it easy this weekend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'm still tired.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Take it easy today.

cards.usageNote: Encourages someone's confidence.
examples: You've got this—just stay focused.
The interview is tough, but you've got this.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'm nervous about the test.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You've got this!

cards.usageNote: Expresses pride in someone's effort or success.
examples: I'm proud of you for trying again.
Your family is proud of you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I finally passed!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm proud of you.

cards.usageNote: Asks someone not to interpret criticism as a personal attack.
examples: Don't take it personally; the rule applies to everyone.
Try not to take it personally if they say no.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: He didn't invite me.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Don't take it personally.

cards.usageNote: Says something does not match your interests or taste.
examples: Camping is fun, but it's not my thing.
That kind of music is not my thing.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Want to go karaoke singing?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's not my thing.

cards.usageNote: Says something is familiar from repeated experience.
examples: I'm used to waking up early.
I'm used to the noise in this neighborhood.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Does the commute bother you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm used to it.

cards.expression: I can't get used to it
cards.usageNote: Says you struggle to become comfortable with something.
examples: I can't get used to this schedule.
She can't get used to the cold weather.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How's the night shift?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I can't get used to it.

cards.usageNote: Makes a sincere promise.
examples: You have my word; I'll be there.
I'll keep it private, you have my word.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I trust you with this?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You have my word.

cards.usageNote: Confirms an agreement or bargain.
examples: I'll cook if you clean; it's a deal.
You help today, I help tomorrow. It's a deal.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'll pay half.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's a deal.

cards.usageNote: Suggests maintaining contact.
examples: Let's keep in touch after graduation.
We should keep in touch even if you move.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'll miss working here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's keep in touch.

cards.usageNote: Informal greeting after a long absence.
examples: Long time no see! How have you been?
I ran into Jay and said, long time no see.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hey, Maya!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Long time no see!

cards.usageNote: Casual farewell common in the United States.
examples: Thanks for stopping by; have a good one.
Have a good one and drive safely.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thanks for the coffee.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You too, have a good one.

cards.usageNote: Casual goodbye suggesting you may meet again.
examples: It was nice talking; see you around.
See you around campus sometime.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'm heading out.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: All right, see you around.

cards.usageNote: Says there is no resentment after disagreement.
examples: No hard feelings about yesterday.
We disagreed, but there are no hard feelings.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sorry about the game.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No hard feelings.

cards.usageNote: Says you unintentionally forgot something.
examples: It slipped my mind that we had plans.
I'm sorry, your birthday slipped my mind.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you send the email?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oh no, it slipped my mind.

cards.usageNote: Suggests deciding what to do as the situation develops.
examples: We don't need a fixed plan; let's play it by ear.
If the weather changes, we can play it by ear.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What time should we leave?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's play it by ear.

cards.usageNote: Thanks someone for a favor and offers to return it.
examples: Thanks for the ride; I owe you one.
You saved my day. I owe you one.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I covered your shift.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks, I owe you one.

cards.tr: Şuna daha yakınım / tercih etmeye eğilimliyim
cards.usageNote: Shows a tentative preference before a decision.
examples: I'm leaning toward the earlier flight.
We're leaning toward renting instead of buying.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Which option do you prefer?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm leaning toward the smaller one.

cards.usageNote: Describes difficulty choosing between two possibilities.
examples: I'm torn between staying and going out.
She's torn between two job offers.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Have you decided where to live?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm torn between downtown and the suburbs.

cards.usageNote: Suggests comparing alternatives before acting.
examples: Let's weigh the options before we commit.
We should weigh the options carefully.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we book the tickets now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's weigh the options first.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges a difficult decision.
examples: Whether to move is a tough call.
It's a tough call with so little information.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Which candidate would you choose?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's a tough call; both are qualified.

cards.usageNote: Offers an informal recommendation or preference.
examples: I'd go with the blue jacket.
For this trip, I'd go with the train.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Which design looks better?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'd go with the second one.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a change of mind.
examples: On second thought, I'll stay home.
Let's take a cab—on second thought, we can walk.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Still want to order pizza?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: On second thought, let's cook.

cards.usageNote: Suggests postponing a decision until tomorrow.
examples: It's expensive; let's sleep on it.
We don't need to decide tonight, so let's sleep on it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we accept the offer?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's sleep on it first.

cards.usageNote: Signals doubts about a decision already made.
examples: I'm having second thoughts about the trip.
She's having second thoughts about quitting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you still buying the car?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm having second thoughts, actually.

cards.usageNote: Reduces a complex issue to its central factor.
examples: It boils down to time and money.
The choice boils down to what matters most.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why did you turn down the offer?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It boils down to the commute.

cards.usageNote: Introduces the most important practical conclusion.
examples: The bottom line is we can't afford it.
The bottom line is that we need more time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What's your final recommendation?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: The bottom line is we should wait.

cards.expression: At the end of the day
cards.usageNote: Highlights an overriding consideration after discussing details.
examples: At the end of the day, it's your choice.
At the end of the day, trust matters.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Does the brand really matter?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: At the end of the day, quality matters more.

cards.usageNote: Frames an opinion without presenting it as fact.
examples: The way I see it, we need a backup plan.
The way I see it, this could work.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we change the schedule?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: The way I see it, we have no choice.

cards.usageNote: Signals a personal viewpoint politely.
examples: From my perspective, the deadline is unrealistic.
The plan looks risky from my perspective.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why are you concerned?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: From my perspective, we're moving too fast.

cards.expression: I see where you're coming from
cards.usageNote: Acknowledges another person's viewpoint without necessarily agreeing.
examples: I see where you're coming from, but I disagree.
I see where you're coming from about the cost.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You don't think the move is worth it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I see where you're coming from, actually.

cards.usageNote: Politely but firmly introduces disagreement; can sound formal.
examples: I beg to differ; the data suggests otherwise.
With respect, I beg to differ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Everyone says this is the best option.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I beg to differ.

cards.usageNote: Expresses doubt about an explanation or proposal.
examples: I'm not convinced the fix will last.
I'm not convinced by that argument.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Does this proposal solve the problem?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm not convinced yet.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges why an option attracts people without fully endorsing it.
examples: I can see the appeal of working from home.
I can see the appeal, but the commute would be long.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do people love that neighborhood?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I can see the appeal.

cards.usageNote: Validates a reasonable worry in a discussion.
examples: That's a fair concern, especially with this budget.
Your concern about privacy is fair.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What about the security risks?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a fair concern.

cards.usageNote: Ends a disagreement without forcing agreement.
examples: We've discussed this enough; let's agree to disagree.
We can agree to disagree and move on.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We're not changing each other's minds.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's agree to disagree.

cards.expression: I wouldn't put it that way
cards.usageNote: Disagrees with someone's wording rather than rejecting the whole idea.
examples: I wouldn't put it that way; it was a misunderstanding.
I wouldn't put it that way, personally.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So the whole project failed?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I wouldn't put it that way.

cards.expression: If you look at it that way
cards.usageNote: Acknowledges how a different framing changes the conclusion.
examples: If you look at it that way, the cost makes sense.
It sounds reasonable if you look at it that way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A longer route gives us more breaks.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: If you look at it that way, sure.

cards.expression: There's more to it than that
cards.usageNote: Says a situation is more complex than it first appears.
examples: There's more to it than that one mistake.
It's not just about price; there's more to it than that.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Was the delay caused by traffic?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's more to it than that.

cards.usageNote: Notes that advice may be difficult to follow.
examples: Saving more money is easier said than done.
Staying calm is easier said than done.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Just stop checking your phone.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's easier said than done.

cards.usageNote: Warns against deciding before the facts are clear.
examples: Let's not jump to conclusions about the delay.
We need evidence; let's not jump to conclusions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you think she ignored us?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's not jump to conclusions.

cards.usageNote: Suggests trying something despite uncertainty.
examples: Let's give it a shot this weekend.
I don't know if it'll work, but let's give it a shot.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we try the new route?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's give it a shot.

cards.tr: İşin püf noktası / gizli şartı ne?
cards.usageNote: Asks whether an attractive offer has a hidden downside.
examples: Free delivery sounds great, but what's the catch?
There's usually a catch with deals like that.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: They're offering a free trial.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: What's the catch?

cards.usageNote: Recommends investigating an idea further.
examples: That scholarship is worth looking into.
The discount might be worth looking into.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we check that apartment?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's worth looking into.

cards.usageNote: Suggests reducing a long list of possibilities.
examples: Let's narrow it down to three hotels.
We should narrow the search down first.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: There are twenty places to choose from.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's narrow it down.

cards.usageNote: Keeps an option open despite uncertainty.
examples: I wouldn't rule out working remotely.
It seems unlikely, but I wouldn't rule it out.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Could we move in December?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I wouldn't rule it out.

cards.usageNote: Identifies the remaining options after eliminating others.
examples: That leaves us with two possible dates.
If both buses are full, that leaves us with the train.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The first hotel is sold out.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That leaves us with the other two.

cards.usageNote: Calls for an honest assessment of limitations.
examples: Let's be realistic about what we can finish.
We need to be realistic about costs.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we finish this by tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's be realistic.

cards.usageNote: Suggests something is expected to happen eventually.
examples: It's only a matter of time before prices rise.
With that much practice, improvement is a matter of time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you think they'll notice?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's a matter of time.

cards.usageNote: Says the outcome cannot be known yet.
examples: Time will tell whether the plan works.
Only time will tell if we chose well.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will the new routine help?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Time will tell.

cards.usageNote: Warns that little time remains for a task.
examples: We're running out of time to register.
We're running out of time before the train leaves.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we stop for coffee?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We're running out of time.

cards.usageNote: Says there is barely enough time for something.
examples: We're cutting it close with a ten-minute transfer.
The deadline is tomorrow; we're cutting it close.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will we make the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We're cutting it close.

cards.expression: Let's get straight to the point
cards.usageNote: Suggests discussing the main issue without a long introduction.
examples: Let's get straight to the point: the rent is too high.
We only have five minutes, so let's get straight to the point.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should I explain the background first?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's get straight to the point.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a simpler explanation of a complex idea.
examples: To put it simply, we need more storage.
To put it simply, the system saves your progress.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What does the update actually do?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: To put it simply, it runs faster.

cards.usageNote: Restates an idea to make it clearer.
examples: In other words, we have to start over.
The plan is flexible; in other words, dates can change.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So we can't apply today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: In other words, we need another document.

cards.usageNote: Makes a position or fact explicit, sometimes defensively.
examples: For the record, I supported the original idea.
For the record, no one was blamed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you agree to the change?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: For the record, I had reservations.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a practical guideline rather than a strict rule.
examples: As a rule of thumb, arrive ten minutes early.
As a rule of thumb, keep a little money aside.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How early should we leave?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: As a rule of thumb, half an hour early.

cards.usageNote: Signals a broad statement with possible exceptions.
examples: Generally speaking, mornings are quieter here.
Generally speaking, the service is reliable.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is public transport expensive?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Generally speaking, no.

cards.usageNote: Softens an opinion or piece of advice.
examples: For what it's worth, I liked your first draft.
For what it's worth, the smaller room felt brighter.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Which one would you pick?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: For what it's worth, I'd choose the first.

cards.usageNote: Politely invites someone to correct a possible mistake.
examples: Correct me if I'm wrong, but the meeting is on Thursday.
Correct me if I'm wrong; you moved last year, right?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We met in June, didn't we?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but it was July.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a request or statement to remove confusion.
examples: Just to clarify, the price includes tax.
Just to clarify, are you coming tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Does this cover both tickets?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Just to clarify, it covers one.

cards.expression: Let me put it another way
cards.usageNote: Restates something after it was not understood.
examples: Let me put it another way: we need a simpler process.
I wasn't clear; let me put it another way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I don't follow your explanation.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let me put it another way.

cards.usageNote: Introduces an important point, often a complication.
examples: Here's the thing: I can't stay late tonight.
Here's the thing, the hotel is already booked.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we leave early tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Here's the thing: I have an appointment.

cards.expression: What I'm trying to say is
cards.usageNote: Helps explain the real point behind someone's words.
examples: What I'm trying to say is that we need a break.
What I'm trying to say is, I appreciate your help.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you saying I made a mistake?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: What I'm trying to say is we can improve.

cards.usageNote: Suggests resolving smaller outstanding issues before finalizing a plan.
examples: Let's iron out the details before we book.
We need to iron out a few details first.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we announce the plan now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's iron out the details first.

cards.expression: Could you walk me through it?
cards.usageNote: Politely requests a step-by-step explanation.
examples: Could you walk me through the setup?
Could you walk me through what happened yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I haven't used this tool before.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Could you walk me through it?

cards.usageNote: Says an explanation is hard to understand.
examples: I'm having trouble following the last part.
I'm having trouble following your explanation.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Does my explanation make sense?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm having trouble following, actually.

cards.expression: Let's take it from the top
cards.usageNote: Suggests restarting an explanation or activity from the beginning.
examples: Let's take it from the top and check each step.
We missed a detail, so let's take it from the top.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Where did the mistake happen?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's take it from the top.

cards.usageNote: Asks someone for a quick summary of essential details.
examples: Give me the rundown when you get back.
Can you give me the rundown before the call?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What happened at the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Give me the rundown.

cards.usageNote: Asks to be included in updates and decisions.
examples: Keep me in the loop about the repairs.
Please keep me in the loop if plans change.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'll speak to the landlord tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Great, keep me in the loop.

cards.usageNote: Shows full attention and willingness to listen.
examples: You've got news? I'm all ears.
If you have suggestions, I'm all ears.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I tell you an idea?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm all ears.

cards.usageNote: Warns that information is uncertain or unofficial.
examples: I think the shop opens at nine, but don't quote me on that.
It might rain tomorrow; don't quote me on that.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is the event definitely on Friday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I think so, but don't quote me on that.

cards.usageNote: Introduces information circulating as rumor, not confirmed fact.
examples: Word has it that the café is closing.
Word has it that they're moving abroad.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why is everyone talking about that building?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Word has it that it's been sold.

cards.usageNote: Expresses surprise at information you did not know.
examples: They're changing the timetable? That's news to me.
That's news to me; nobody mentioned it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Didn't you hear about the policy?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's news to me.

cards.expression: I heard it through the grapevine
cards.usageNote: Says you learned something informally through other people.
examples: I heard through the grapevine that she's moving.
I heard it through the grapevine, so it may be wrong.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How did you find out about the party?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I heard it through the grapevine.

cards.usageNote: Says something sounds familiar but details are unclear.
examples: Her name rings a bell.
That address rings a bell, but I can't place it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Have you heard of that restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That rings a bell.

cards.usageNote: Says something does not sound familiar.
examples: That title doesn't ring a bell.
Sorry, the name doesn't ring a bell.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you know this artist?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It doesn't ring a bell.

cards.usageNote: Means you have not chosen a side or option yet.
examples: I'm on the fence about joining the class.
I'm still on the fence about the move.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you coming with us?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm on the fence.

cards.usageNote: Says a decision is now final.
examples: I've made up my mind about the apartment.
She's made up her mind to leave.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you still thinking about it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, I've made up my mind.

cards.usageNote: Names a condition that makes an option unacceptable.
examples: A two-hour commute is a deal-breaker for me.
No refund policy? That's a deal-breaker.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Would you rent that place?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not without heating. That's a deal-breaker.

cards.usageNote: Accepts an imperfect but tolerable solution.
examples: The room is small, but I can live with that.
An extra ten minutes? I can live with that.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The flight leaves at six.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I can live with that.

cards.usageNote: Shows readiness to accept a middle-ground solution.
examples: I'm willing to compromise on the location.
We're willing to compromise if it helps.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You want to leave early, but I want to stay.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm willing to compromise.

cards.usageNote: Offers a compromise between different preferences.
examples: Let's meet halfway and leave at eight.
We could meet halfway on the price.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want Saturday, you want Monday.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's meet halfway and choose Sunday.

cards.usageNote: Asks whether a mutually acceptable arrangement is possible.
examples: Can we work something out with the landlord?
If the date is a problem, can we work something out?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I can't pay everything today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Can we work something out?

cards.usageNote: Strongly rejects an option as unacceptable.
examples: Skipping the safety check is out of the question.
Leaving the door unlocked is out of the question.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Could we cancel without telling anyone?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's out of the question.

cards.usageNote: Says a plan or decision can still change.
examples: The schedule isn't set in stone.
Our plans aren't set in stone yet.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we change the dinner time?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sure, it's not set in stone.

cards.usageNote: Suggests not committing too early.
examples: Let's keep our options open until Friday.
We should keep our options open for the trip.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we book the first hotel?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's keep our options open.

cards.usageNote: Politely requests advance warning.
examples: I'd appreciate a heads-up before visitors arrive.
Next time, I'd appreciate a heads-up.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I change the plan tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sure, but I'd appreciate a heads-up.

cards.tr: Son anda haber verdiğim için üzgünüm
cards.usageNote: Apologizes for giving someone little advance warning.
examples: Sorry for the short notice, but I can't attend.
Sorry for the short notice about the schedule change.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I only found out just now.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No problem. Thanks for the heads-up.

cards.usageNote: Thanks someone for staying patient during a delay or difficulty.
examples: Thanks for bearing with me while I checked.
Thanks for bearing with me this morning.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That took longer than expected.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks for bearing with me.

cards.expression: I appreciate you bringing that up
cards.usageNote: Politely recognizes a useful point someone raised.
examples: I appreciate you bringing that up in the meeting.
I appreciate you bringing that up; I hadn't considered it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think there's a privacy risk.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I appreciate you bringing that up.

cards.expression: Sorry to put you on the spot
cards.usageNote: Apologizes for demanding an immediate response in public or unexpectedly.
examples: Sorry to put you on the spot with that question.
I didn't mean to put you on the spot.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do I have to answer right now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, sorry to put you on the spot.

cards.usageNote: Reassures someone that they do not have to agree.
examples: You can join us, but no pressure at all.
No pressure at all if you're busy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do I have to decide today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No pressure at all.

cards.usageNote: Defers to someone else's schedule or preference.
examples: We can meet online or in person—whatever works best for you.
Pick a time, whatever works best for you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Morning or afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Whatever works best for you.

cards.usageNote: Asks permission politely and indirectly.
examples: Would you mind if I opened the window?
Would you mind if I joined the call a little late?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The room feels hot.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Would you mind if I opened the window?

cards.usageNote: Softens a request or question to sound less direct.
examples: I was wondering if we could reschedule.
I was wondering if you had any recommendations.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What can I help you with?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I was wondering if you have a table for two.

cards.expression: Could you do me a favor?
cards.usageNote: Politely asks someone to help with something.
examples: Could you do me a favor and check the door?
Could you do me a favor this afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you have a minute?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Actually, could you do me a favor?

cards.usageNote: Softens a potentially inconvenient request.
examples: I hate to ask, but could you stay ten minutes?
I hate to ask, but can we change seats?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Everything okay?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I hate to ask, but could you lend me your charger?

cards.usageNote: Shows concern about taking up someone's time or space.
examples: I don't want to impose on your weekend.
I don't want to impose, so I'll take a taxi.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You can stay at our place.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks, but I don't want to impose.

cards.usageNote: Warmly offers permission or an invitation.
examples: You're more than welcome to stay for dinner.
You're more than welcome to ask questions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I bring my sister?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You're more than welcome to.

cards.usageNote: Invites someone to contact you if needed.
examples: Feel free to reach out with questions.
If anything changes, feel free to reach out.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What if I need help later?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Feel free to reach out.

cards.usageNote: Expresses sincere gratitude for help or kindness.
examples: You stayed late for me; I really appreciate it.
I really appreciate your patience.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I fixed your reservation.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks, I really appreciate it.

cards.expression: You didn't have to do that
cards.usageNote: Thanks someone warmly for an unexpected kindness.
examples: You brought me coffee? You didn't have to do that.
You didn't have to do that, but it's so kind.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I picked up your groceries.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You didn't have to do that!

cards.expression: That means a lot to me
cards.tr: Bu benim için çok şey ifade ediyor
cards.usageNote: Responds to words or actions that feel personally meaningful.
examples: Your support means a lot to me.
Hearing that really means a lot to me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We're proud of your progress.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That means a lot to me.

cards.expression: I couldn't have done it without you
cards.usageNote: Credits someone for important help in achieving something.
examples: I couldn't have done it without your advice.
We couldn't have done it without the team.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Congratulations on finishing!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thanks! I couldn't have done it without you.

cards.usageNote: Offers or acknowledges help in a friendly way.
examples: I'm happy to help with the forms.
If you need another hand, I'm happy to help.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thanks for checking the details.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm happy to help.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a sincere apology for a mistake.
examples: I owe you an apology for yesterday.
I owe you an apology; I misunderstood.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why did you call me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I owe you an apology.

cards.usageNote: Accepts accountability for a mistake or outcome.
examples: I take full responsibility for the error.
She took full responsibility for the delay.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Who sent the wrong file?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I did, and I take full responsibility.

cards.usageNote: Suggests moving on after a disagreement or mistake.
examples: We talked it through; let's put it behind us.
I'd like to put the argument behind us.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you still upset?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No. Let's put it behind us.

cards.expression: There's no point dwelling on it
cards.usageNote: Discourages repeatedly focusing on something unchangeable.
examples: There's no point dwelling on yesterday's mistake.
It's over; there's no point dwelling on it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I keep thinking about that conversation.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's no point dwelling on it.

cards.usageNote: Expresses surprise at an unexpected event.
examples: I didn't see that coming at all.
The sudden announcement? I didn't see that coming.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: She quit this morning.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Wow, I didn't see that coming.

cards.usageNote: Says an event or question was unexpected.
examples: The question caught me off guard.
His reaction really caught me off guard.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why did you pause during the interview?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That caught me off guard.

cards.usageNote: Shows strong positive amazement or surprise.
examples: I'm blown away by how much you've improved.
The view absolutely blew me away.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you like the performance?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm blown away.

cards.usageNote: Describes intense surprise at something seen.
examples: I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the snow.
The room was so different I couldn't believe my eyes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Was the renovation impressive?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I couldn't believe my eyes.

cards.usageNote: Expresses inability to understand someone's behavior or a situation.
examples: Why he left without telling us is beyond me.
It's beyond me how they finished so quickly.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why did they ignore the warning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's beyond me.

cards.usageNote: Shows that you have experienced something similar.
examples: I can relate to that feeling of uncertainty.
I can relate to that; moving is stressful.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I get nervous before interviews.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I can relate to that.

cards.usageNote: Empathizes with a feeling you have personally experienced.
examples: I know the feeling after a long week.
I know the feeling of missing home.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I'm exhausted after today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I know the feeling.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges that someone else's experience seems difficult.
examples: That sounds frustrating, especially after waiting so long.
Being ignored like that sounds frustrating.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: They canceled my appointment again.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That sounds frustrating.

cards.usageNote: Recognizes that someone's worry has likely ended.
examples: You must be relieved the results are in.
You must be relieved to be home.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: They finally found my luggage.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You must be relieved.

cards.usageNote: Shows sympathy when you have not personally experienced the situation.
examples: I can only imagine how tiring that was.
I can only imagine what you're going through.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The move was incredibly stressful.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I can only imagine.

cards.usageNote: Says someone's reaction is understandable.
examples: I don't blame you for wanting a break.
You left early? I don't blame you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I didn't want to argue with him.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I don't blame you.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges difficult experiences someone has faced.
examples: You've been through a lot this year.
You've been through a lot; take some time off.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I feel exhausted lately.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: You've been through a lot.

cards.expression: Don't be too hard on yourself
cards.usageNote: Encourages someone not to judge their own mistakes harshly.
examples: Don't be too hard on yourself over one mistake.
You're learning; don't be too hard on yourself.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I can't believe I forgot.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Don't be too hard on yourself.

cards.usageNote: Encourages someone to recognize their own achievement.
examples: Give yourself some credit; you worked hard.
You did well, so give yourself some credit.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It wasn't that impressive.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Give yourself some credit!

cards.usageNote: Says adapting to a new situation is gradual.
examples: It takes time to adjust to a new city.
It takes time to adjust after changing jobs.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I still feel strange here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It takes time to adjust.

cards.expression: I'm getting the hang of it
cards.usageNote: Indicates that a skill is beginning to feel easier.
examples: I'm getting the hang of driving here.
After a week, I'm getting the hang of it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How's the new software?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm getting the hang of it.

cards.usageNote: Admits a skill has weakened because of lack of practice.
examples: I'm a little rusty at speaking French.
I haven't played in years, so I'm rusty.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you still play the piano?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm a little rusty.

cards.usageNote: Suggests changing the way a problem is handled.
examples: Let's take a different approach to this lesson.
We need to take a different approach to planning.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The current method isn't working.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's take a different approach.

cards.usageNote: Recognizes improvement even if the goal is not yet reached.
examples: We're making progress on the repairs.
We're making progress, one step at a time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are we any closer to finishing?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We're making progress.

cards.expression: It's a step in the right direction
cards.usageNote: Praises a positive change that is not yet a complete solution.
examples: The new policy is a step in the right direction.
It's a step in the right direction, even if it's small.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The process is still slow.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: True, but it's a step in the right direction.

cards.usageNote: Says a failed attempt means starting again.
examples: The files were lost, so we're back to square one.
If the deal falls through, we're back to square one.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did the repair work?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, we're back to square one.

cards.usageNote: Expresses suspicion that facts or numbers do not make sense together.
examples: Something doesn't add up in this bill.
Her story sounds odd; something doesn't add up.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why are the totals different?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Something doesn't add up.

cards.usageNote: Suggests verifying details to prevent mistakes.
examples: Let's double-check the address before leaving.
We should double-check the total.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Are you sure this is the right gate?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's double-check.

cards.expression: Let's get to the bottom of it
cards.usageNote: Suggests investigating a problem until the cause is clear.
examples: Let's get to the bottom of the noise complaint.
We need to get to the bottom of this error.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why does the bill keep changing?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's get to the bottom of it.

cards.usageNote: Reassures someone that a practical problem is manageable.
examples: We can sort this out with a quick call.
Don't worry, we can sort this out.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The reservation is under the wrong name.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We can sort this out.

cards.expression: It's not going according to plan
cards.usageNote: Describes events that differ from what was expected.
examples: The trip isn't going according to plan.
Nothing is going according to plan today.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why are you still at the airport?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's not going according to plan.

cards.expression: Let's make the most of it
cards.usageNote: Suggests using a less-than-ideal situation positively.
examples: It's raining, but let's make the most of it.
We have only an hour, so let's make the most of it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The beach is closed.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's make the most of it.

cards.expression: I wouldn't go so far as to say
cards.usageNote: Qualifies a judgment without rejecting it completely.
examples: I wouldn't go so far as to say the event was a failure.
I wouldn't go so far as to say we were misled.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: So the whole project was a disaster?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I wouldn't go so far as to say that.

cards.expression: There's a case to be made for
cards.usageNote: Recognizes that an option has reasonable supporting arguments.
examples: There's a case to be made for moving closer to work.
There's a case to be made for waiting another year.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why would anyone choose the longer route?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's a case to be made for it.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a cautious opinion rather than a firm conclusion.
examples: I'm inclined to think the delay was accidental.
I'm inclined to think we need more information.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you think they're upset?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm inclined to think it's a misunderstanding.

cards.usageNote: Says an outcome is still uncertain despite claims.
examples: Whether the change helps remains to be seen.
That remains to be seen after the first month.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will the new plan save money?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That remains to be seen.

cards.usageNote: Says a situation lacks an obvious simple answer.
examples: The decision isn't entirely clear-cut.
It's not entirely clear-cut who is responsible.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is one option clearly better?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's not entirely clear-cut.

cards.usageNote: Partly acknowledges a claim while allowing qualifications.
examples: There's some truth to that, but the context matters.
I think there's some truth to that criticism.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is the city really getting too expensive?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's some truth to that.

cards.usageNote: Signals a specific objection to someone's statement or behavior.
examples: I take issue with how the decision was explained.
I take issue with the assumption behind that claim.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You disagree with the whole plan?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, I take issue with the timeline.

cards.usageNote: Rejects an unsupported inference from a previous point.
examples: Prices rose, but that doesn't necessarily follow from demand.
That doesn't necessarily follow from what she said.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: He was quiet, so he must be upset.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That doesn't necessarily follow.

cards.expression: That's a bit of a stretch
cards.usageNote: Describes a claim as going beyond reasonable evidence.
examples: Calling it a conspiracy is a bit of a stretch.
That explanation feels like a bit of a stretch.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: He missed one call, so he's avoiding us.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That's a bit of a stretch.

cards.usageNote: Reminds people of an important goal amid details.
examples: Let's not lose sight of why we started.
We shouldn't lose sight of the people affected.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: We're debating tiny design choices.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's not lose sight of the main goal.

cards.usageNote: Introduces context that helps judge an event's importance.
examples: To put things into perspective, the delay was only a day.
To put things into perspective, the rent includes utilities.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is the price increase huge?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: To put things into perspective, it's less than inflation.

cards.expression: When you put it that way
cards.usageNote: Acknowledges that a new framing affects your response.
examples: When you put it that way, I understand your concern.
It sounds reasonable when you put it that way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: It's about keeping the team safe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: When you put it that way, I agree.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a stronger or contrasting point, often correcting an assumption.
examples: The trip wasn't exhausting; if anything, it was refreshing.
If anything, the change made things easier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did the feedback discourage you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: If anything, it motivated me.

cards.usageNote: Identifies one worthwhile benefit or action.
examples: If nothing else, we'll learn from the attempt.
If nothing else, call to say you're safe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will the visit really be useful?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: If nothing else, we'll see the place.

cards.usageNote: Introduces something learned later that changes an earlier impression.
examples: As it turns out, the museum is closed on Mondays.
As it turns out, she already knew.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Was the café still open?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: As it turns out, it closed early.

cards.usageNote: Introduces something recalled while speaking.
examples: Come to think of it, I haven't seen him lately.
Come to think of it, we never confirmed the address.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did we lock the car?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Come to think of it, I'm not sure.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges information prompted by someone else's comment.
examples: Now that you mention it, the room did feel cold.
Now that you mention it, I heard that too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wasn't the restaurant quieter last year?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Now that you mention it, yes.

cards.tr: Bildiğim kadarıyla / benim bilmediğim bir durumda
cards.usageNote: Stresses uncertainty about what might be true.
examples: For all I know, the package could already be here.
He may be on vacation, for all I know.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Where did she go?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: For all I know, she's still at the office.

cards.usageNote: Gives a cautious negative answer without claiming complete knowledge.
examples: There haven't been any changes, not that I'm aware of.
Not that I'm aware of, but I can check.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did anyone cancel the meeting?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not that I'm aware of.

cards.usageNote: States one's personal position or decision on a matter.
examples: As far as I'm concerned, we can leave now.
As far as I'm concerned, the matter is settled.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do we still need to discuss it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: As far as I'm concerned, no.

cards.usageNote: Points out that a discussion ignores its broader context.
examples: We're missing the bigger picture by focusing on minor delays.
If we only discuss price, we're missing the bigger picture.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why not just change the colors?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We're missing the bigger picture.

cards.usageNote: Says a discussion fails because participants address different points.
examples: We're talking past each other about the deadline.
I think we're talking past each other here.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why can't we agree?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We're talking past each other.

cards.usageNote: Says a discussion repeats without progress.
examples: We've been going around in circles for an hour.
This debate is going around in circles.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we discuss it again?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, we're going around in circles.

cards.usageNote: Suggests reconsidering the broader situation before proceeding.
examples: Let's take a step back and review the goal.
We need to take a step back before choosing.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Which button should we redesign?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's take a step back first.

cards.usageNote: Invites a closer analysis of a complex statement.
examples: Let's unpack that assumption before acting.
That's a big claim; let's unpack that.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I think the system is unfair.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's unpack that.

cards.expression: It comes down to a judgment call
cards.usageNote: Says there is no perfectly objective way to decide.
examples: It comes down to a judgment call about timing.
Without clear evidence, it's a judgment call.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we prove which design is best?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, it comes down to a judgment call.

cards.expression: That's where I draw the line
cards.usageNote: Names a limit that you are unwilling to cross.
examples: I can work late, but unpaid weekends are where I draw the line.
That's where I draw the line on privacy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Would you share your password for convenience?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, that's where I draw the line.

cards.usageNote: Sets a boundary without directly accusing others.
examples: I'm not comfortable with sharing that information.
I wasn't comfortable with the way he spoke to her.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can I post your photo online?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I'm not comfortable with that.

cards.usageNote: Signals concern about exceeding one's role or authority.
examples: I don't want to overstep, but may I offer advice?
I didn't want to overstep by making that choice.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why didn't you change the schedule?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I didn't want to overstep.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges competing perspectives in a disagreement.
examples: I can see both sides of the debate.
I can see both sides, which makes this difficult.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Whose argument do you support?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I can see both sides.

cards.expression: Let's give them the benefit of the doubt
cards.usageNote: Suggests assuming good intentions until evidence says otherwise.
examples: Let's give them the benefit of the doubt for now.
I try to give people the benefit of the doubt.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: He hasn't replied in two days.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Let's give him the benefit of the doubt.

cards.expression: I wouldn't read too much into it
cards.usageNote: Advises against overinterpreting an ambiguous detail.
examples: I wouldn't read too much into that comment.
She looked distracted, but I wouldn't read too much into it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: He didn't smile when he saw me.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I wouldn't read too much into it.

cards.expression: Take that with a grain of salt
cards.usageNote: Warns that information may be unreliable or exaggerated.
examples: Take that rumor with a grain of salt.
I'd take the online review with a grain of salt.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Someone said the shop is closing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Take that with a grain of salt.

cards.usageNote: Acknowledges an unavoidable fact or problem.
examples: There's no getting around the cost of repairs.
There's no getting around it: we need more time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Could we skip the inspection?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's no getting around it.

cards.usageNote: Emphasizes that a detail is too important to ignore.
examples: We can't afford to overlook the safety risks.
We can't afford to overlook customer feedback.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do these small errors matter?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We can't afford to overlook them.

cards.usageNote: Means the consequences of a decision are especially important.
examples: The stakes are high when personal data is involved.
The stakes are high for everyone affected.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why do we need another review?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Because the stakes are high.

cards.usageNote: Describes competing needs that must be managed carefully.
examples: It's a delicate balance between speed and accuracy.
Work and family can be a delicate balance.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can we improve speed without losing quality?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's a delicate balance.

cards.usageNote: Warns that the justification or situation is not secure.
examples: We're on shaky ground without written confirmation.
That argument puts us on shaky ground.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Should we make the announcement now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We're on shaky ground without the facts.

cards.expression: That puts things in a different light
cards.usageNote: Indicates that new information changes how a situation is judged.
examples: That detail puts the disagreement in a different light.
Her explanation put things in a different light.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: He was helping his neighbor all morning.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: That puts things in a different light.

cards.expression: There's a lot to be said for
cards.usageNote: Appreciates the benefits of a choice, often against alternatives.
examples: There's a lot to be said for living close to work.
There's a lot to be said for keeping things simple.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Why not buy a larger house?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: There's a lot to be said for having less debt.

cards.usageNote: Warns that an uncertain event is not safe to depend on.
examples: I wouldn't bank on getting a refund.
The weather might improve, but I wouldn't bank on it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will the tickets get cheaper?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I wouldn't bank on it.

cards.usageNote: Suggests something is unlikely to happen soon.
examples: Don't hold your breath for an immediate reply.
They may fix it, but don't hold your breath.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Do you think he'll apologize?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Don't hold your breath.

cards.usageNote: Says two opposite outcomes are equally plausible.
examples: The vote could go either way.
With this weather, the game could go either way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Who do you think will win?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It could go either way.

cards.usageNote: Says no one has enough information to predict the outcome.
examples: When they'll reopen is anyone's guess.
It's anyone's guess how long the repair will take.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: When will prices drop?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's anyone's guess.

cards.usageNote: Sets a limit on agreement or acceptability.
examples: I agree with you, but only to a point.
The approach works, but only to a point.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Does the new rule solve everything?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Only to a point.

cards.usageNote: Introduces a balanced overall assessment.
examples: All things considered, the trip went well.
All things considered, I'd take the job.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Was the apartment worth the price?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: All things considered, yes.

cards.usageNote: Concludes after considering positives and negatives.
examples: On balance, I think we made the right choice.
The changes have helped on balance.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Would you recommend that school?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: On balance, yes.

cards.usageNote: Describes what is mostly true, allowing exceptions.
examples: By and large, the neighborhood is quiet.
The feedback was positive by and large.
